newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel little moved by Inco strike deal.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel little moved by Inco strike deal.

text.p: Three months delivery nickel prices failed to show any serious reaction on Friday to news that union negotiators at Canada's Inco Ltd had endorsed a contract deal to end a four-week strike.
At 0730 GMT nickel was indicated at $7,040/70 a tonne, against Thursday's LME kerb close of $7,070.
The union at Inco's Sudbury, Ontario, division said a ratification vote on the deal would be held on Saturday. Results of the vote would be announced late that afternoon.
According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce 230 million pounds of nickel and 200 million pounds of copper this year.
"Nickel has not fallen out of bed...the news was already factored in," one LME trader said.
Traders were more concerned about the copper market which can spark wide gyrations in nickel. Copper is expected to be choppy on Friday.
"The next move for nickel is in the hands of the copper market," the trader added.
Traders also expected LME nickel stocks to rise on Friday.
"Another build could be enough to send prices south," another trader commented.
